            <h2 class="section-heading">Introduction</h2>
            <p>Matías Deneken is a Chilean sociologist and <span class="kw kw--data">data scientist</span> whose work sits at the intersection of the <span class="kw kw--violence">sociology of violence</span>, <span class="kw kw--democracy">democracy</span>, and <span class="kw kw--computational">computational social science</span>. His research examines how social processes unfold in contemporary societies through the rigorous application of <span class="kw kw--methods">quantitative and computational methods</span>.

<h2 class="section-heading">Milestones</h2>
<p>His graduate studies have been fully funded by Chile's <strong>National Agency for Research and Development (ANID)</strong> — the national equivalent of UKRI or the U.S. NSF — through its <strong>International Doctoral Scholarship</strong> (2026–2030), ranked first in the <span class="kw kw--ai">Artificial Intelligence</span> area, and its <strong>National Master's Scholarship</strong> (2022–2024). He also received a <strong>Fulbright Equal Opportunity Scholarship</strong> (declined) and the <strong>University of Concepción Award</strong> for academic excellence in Sociology (2022).</p>

            <p>Matías founded <strong><a href="https://www.methodolab.com" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">MethodoLab</a></strong> — a data science initiative that pushes the <span class="kw kw--cream">frontier of computational methods in social research</span> through consultancy, pipelines, and applied analytics for academic and public-sector projects.</p>
